fixture_purpose: Cross-character starting-individuality pressure. Semantic/content evidence only; not a runtime automated personality score.

must_remain_distinct_through: attention to who obeys whom and which familiar adults remain reliable
strangers and movement evaluated first through familiar adults' reactions
discomfort when partly-understood adult matters are dismissed without explanation
interest in family stories, names, writing traces and familiar household learning
tendency to stay near trusted relatives in unfamiliar adult groups before joining
conflicting adult explanations taken back to a trusted elder rather than resolved as mature analysis
household change felt first as disruption of familiar care/learning routine

blind_review_acceptance: Remove character names, aliases, adult titles and future-history references.
A reviewer can still describe two materially different childhood starting persons from family ecology, attention pattern, information source, relationships and stress response.
The distinction is not reducible to age labels or generic class stereotypes; authored completion contains character-specific, revisable dispositions.

Counterfactual-adult test: if the reviewer did not know either person's famous adulthood, each authored completion would still be plausible from the pre-T0 ecology and would not look like a hidden prophecy.
Multi-future test: each starting profile can plausibly grow into at least several materially different adult personalities under different lived histories.
Neither profile contains a hidden requirement to converge on the historical adult.
failure_conditions: Both profiles become interchangeable after names are removed.
Difference is produced mainly by future adult achievements or famous adult stereotypes.
Age/development label substitutes for personality content.
Military-family child or literati-family child is treated as a deterministic class template.
Authored completion is presented as attested historical fact.
A supposedly early trait has been selected mainly because it neatly predicts the known adult.
